books.usage: dd-cli books [list] [--q <s>] [--author <s>] [--series <s>] [--genre <s>] [--start <n>] | facets | get <bookID> [--out <path>] | meta <nodeID> | scan | info
books.long:
DiscoDrive books domain (ebooks).
  list (default)        — library; filters are mutually exclusive (q|author|series|genre), pagination via --start
  facets                — available filter values (authors/series/genres)
  get <bookID> [--out]  — download a book file (bookID — the id field from the list)
  meta <nodeID>         — show book metadata (nodeID — the nodeId field from the list)
  scan                  — start scanning the books folder (in background)
  info                  — show book settings
Note: a book in the list has TWO identifiers — id (for get) and nodeId (for meta).
With --json output is machine-readable.

msg.shown: Shown: {Count} (total={Total}; total is unreliable when filtering)
msg.scan_not_configured: Books folder is not configured — nothing to scan.

cal.usage: dd-cli cal events [--from <t>] [--to <t>] | add --summary <s> --start <t> [flags] | show <uid> | set <uid> [flags] | rm <uid> | calendars
cal.long:
Calendar operations (times — RFC3339, e.g. 2026-07-02T10:00:00Z; a value without a zone is read as local time).
  events [--from <t>] [--to <t>]   — events in a time window (default: today…+7 days)
  add --summary <s> --start <t> [--end <t>] [--location <l>] [--description <d>] [--all-day] [--repeat <daily|weekly|monthly|yearly>] [--until <t>] [--alarm <min>] [--calendar <id>] [--tz <IANA>]  — create an event
  show <uid> [--calendar <id>]     — full details of an event
  set <uid> [flags of add]         — change only the fields given (an empty value clears one)
  rm <uid> [--calendar <id>]       — delete an event (⚠️ Irreversible)
  calendars                        — list calendars
With --json output is machine-readable.

msg.set_no_flags: nothing to change: pass at least one field flag

flag.all_day: all-day event (only the date part of start/end is used)
flag.alarm_set: reminder N minutes before start; "" removes it, "keep" leaves the existing reminders untouched
flag.tz: IANA time zone (for example Europe/Berlin; default: system zone)

contacts.long:
Contact management. list (default) — list contacts show — contact details add --name [--email ] [--phone

] [--org ] — create rm — delete (⚠️ Irreversible) With --json output is machine-readable.

tasks.usage: dd-cli tasks [list] | add --summary <s> [flags] | done <uid> | undone <uid> | rm <uid>
tasks.long:
Task management.
  list (default)        — list tasks (incomplete first)
  add --summary <s> [--due <RFC3339>] [--priority <1..9>]  — create
  done <uid>            — mark done
  undone <uid>          — unmark
  rm <uid>             — delete (⚠️ Irreversible)
With --json output is machine-readable.

music.usage: dd-cli music [radio] | list [subpath] | radio-add --name <n> --stream <url> [--home <url>] | radio-rm <id> | podcasts | podcast-add <feedURL> | podcast-rm <id> | scan | info
music.long:
DiscoDrive music domain.
  radio (default)                — list radio stations
  list [subpath]                 — contents of the music folder (artists/albums/tracks as files);
                                  subpath descends inward, e.g. list "Bi-2/Lunapark"
  radio-add --name --stream [--home]  — add a station
  radio-rm <id>                 — delete a station (⚠️ Irreversible)
  podcasts                      — list podcast subscriptions
  podcast-add <feedURL>         — subscribe to a podcast by feed URL
  podcast-rm <id>               — unsubscribe (⚠️ Irreversible)
  scan                          — start scanning the music folder (in background)
  info                          — show music settings
Note: the full library (search/streaming) is via Subsonic; this is a plain file listing.
With --json output is machine-readable.

msg.need_feed_url: feed URL required: dd-cli music podcast-add <feedURL>
msg.scan_not_configured: Music folder is not configured — nothing to scan.

ls.long:
Prints folder contents by path (default: root). Directories are marked with "/", files show their size.
With --json — an array of {id,name,is_dir,size,version}.

get.long: Downloads a file by path. dest — local path (default: the file name in the current directory; "-" — stdout).

msg.is_dir: {Path} is a folder, not a file

put.long: Uploads a local file to a destination folder. <path> — the destination path (folder/name). The destination folder must exist.

mkdir.long: Creates a folder at the path. The parent folder must exist.

mv.long: Moves or renames a file/folder. If dst is an existing folder, src is moved inside it.

rm.long: Soft-deletes a file or folder (along with its contents). Restore is via the DiscoDrive trash.

share.summary: create a link/access to a node
share.long:
Creates a public link (default) or grants access to a user by email.
--expires accepts a Go duration (e.g. 24h). With --json prints {share_id,token,access}.

flag.email: grant access to a user by email (otherwise — public link)

login.long:
Starts device-code pairing: prints a confirmation link and a short code,
then waits for confirmation on any device where you're logged in to DiscoDrive.
Password/TOTP is never typed into the terminal (works for passkey accounts and on headless machines too).
After logging in, offers to register the dd-mcp MCP server in the Claude config (--no-claude disables this).

flag.name: device name
flag.no_claude: don't register dd-mcp in the Claude config
flag.allow_changes: allow changing tools in the Claude config
flag.insecure: skip TLS certificate verification (self-signed server); saved into the profile

msg.claude_setup_failed: warning: failed to register dd-mcp in Claude

logout.summary: log out: revoke the device on the server and forget the profile
logout.long:
Breaks the pairing: revokes the current device on the server (the device-token becomes
invalid) and removes the profile from the local cli.json.
  --local-only — don't contact the server, only forget the local profile
                 (e.g. if the token was already revoked in the web UI).

flag.local_only: don't revoke the device on the server, only forget the profile

msg.revoke_failed: warning: failed to revoke the device on the server
msg.revoke_manual_hint: revoke it manually in the DiscoDrive web UI (the "Devices" section).

whoami.long: Prints the current user's email, role, and id (GET /me). With --json — an object {id,email,role,tenant_id}.

setup_claude.summary: register dd-mcp in Claude config(s); toggle change mode
setup_claude.long:
Finds dd-mcp and adds it as an MCP server to existing Claude Desktop/Code configs.
  --allow-changes — allow changing tools (delete/move, etc.)
  no flag          — read-only mode (changing tools disabled)
Running again with/without the flag toggles the mode. Restart Claude after switching.

print_config.summary: print a dd-mcp registration snippet for any MCP client
print_config.long:
Prints a ready-to-paste dd-mcp registration snippet — doesn't change anything on disk.
Unlike setup-claude (which edits Claude configs), this works for any MCP client
(Cursor, Zed, Cline, ChatGPT connectors, etc.).
  no flags         — stdio variant (JSON mcpServers) for local clients
  --http <addr>    — variant for HTTP clients: the run command + URL
  --allow-changes  — include changing tools in the printed snippet

example.1: dd-cli print-config --allow-changes          # stdio with changing tools
example.2: dd-cli print-config --http 127.0.0.1:8080    # variant for ChatGPT/remote clients

flag.allow_changes: include changing tools in the output
flag.http: print the variant for HTTP clients (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080)

msg.http_header: HTTP transport — for clients that work over a URL (ChatGPT connectors, remote access):
msg.http_creds:
Credentials come from the profile (dd-cli login) or the DISCODRIVE_SERVER/DISCODRIVE_TOKEN env
vars on the server side — the client only needs the URL. The MCP layer has no authentication:
keep the port local or restrict access at the network/proxy level.
msg.stdio_header:
Paste into your MCP client config (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, Zed, etc.):

{Snippet}
msg.stdio_creds1: Credentials — from the profile (dd-cli login), or add to the env entry:
msg.stdio_footer: For HTTP clients (e.g. ChatGPT): dd-cli print-config --http 127.0.0.1:8080

rename.long: Renames a file or folder in place (keeps it in the same folder). <new-name> is a bare name, not a path — to move between folders, use `mv`.

msg.name_has_slash: <new-name> must be a name, not a path (use `mv` to move): {Name}

bookmarks.summary: browser bookmarks: tree, add, edit, delete
bookmarks.usage: dd-cli bookmarks [tree] | list [flags] | add <url> [flags] | mkdir <title> [flags] | edit <id> [flags] | rm <id>
bookmarks.long:
Browser bookmarks synced from the extension.
  tree (default)        — the whole tree, id in the first column
  list [--q <s>] [--folder <f>] [--folders]  — flat list with folder paths
  add <url> [--title <s>] [--parent <f>] [--position <n>]  — new bookmark
  mkdir <title> [--parent <f>]  — new folder
  edit <id> [--title <s>] [--url <u>] [--parent <f>] [--position <n>]  — rename or move
  rm <id>               — delete, a folder together with its contents (⚠️ Irreversible)
A folder <f> is either an id or a path such as "Toolbar/Dev".
Only the flags you type are sent, so --parent "" is a deliberate move to the top level.
With --json output is machine-readable.

example.3: dd-cli bookmarks add https://go.dev --title Go --parent "Bookmarks Toolbar/Dev"
example.4: dd-cli bookmarks edit b7f8g9 --title "The Go site"

flag.q: substring of the title, the url or the folder path
flag.folder: limit to this folder and everything under it: an id or a path like "Toolbar/Dev"
flag.title: title
flag.parent: parent folder: an id or a path like "Toolbar/Dev"; empty = top level
flag.parent_move: move into this folder: an id or a path like "Toolbar/Dev"; pass an empty value to move to the top level
flag.position: position among siblings (default: after the last one)

msg.nothing_to_change: nothing to change: pass at least one of --title, --url, --parent, --position

pocket.summary: read-later articles: list, add, read, delete
pocket.usage: dd-cli pocket [list] [flags] | add <url> [--title <s>] | read <id> [--out <file>] | retry <id> | rm <id>
pocket.long:
Read-later articles. The server fetches and converts a page in the background,
so a fresh item starts as pending.
  list (default)        — newest first; --status <s> --q <s> --limit <n> --offset <n>
  add <url> [--title <s>]  — save a page
  read <id> [--out <file>]  — the markdown, to stdout or to a file
  retry <id>            — fetch it again (for status error)
  rm <id>               — delete; the markdown file already written stays (⚠️ Irreversible)
Server-side downloads are never listed here — see dd-cli download.
With --json output is machine-readable.

flag.status: filter by status: pending, processing, done or error
flag.q: substring of the title or the url
flag.title: title override; ignored if this url is already saved
flag.out: write the markdown to this file instead of stdout

download.long:
Downloads that the server performs into your Downloads folder.
  add <url> [--title <s>] [--cookie <s>]  — queue it; the transfer runs on the server
  status <id>           — progress of one download
  list (default)        — the downloads this machine queued
  rm <id>               — stop it and forget the queue entry; bytes already
                          written stay as a file (⚠️ Irreversible)
The server keeps no list of downloads and forgets finished ones, so list reads a
local journal in downloads.json next to cli.json; ids queued elsewhere are not in it.
With --json output is machine-readable.

flag.title: label for the queue entry
flag.cookie: Cookie header for a site behind a login

msg.journal_empty: No downloads queued from this machine.
msg.journal_failed: warning: could not update the local download journal: {Msg}

flag.http: print the variant for HTTP clients (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080)

msg.http_creds:
Credentials come from the profile (dd-mcp login) or the DISCODRIVE_SERVER/DISCODRIVE_TOKEN env
vars on the server side — the client only needs the URL. The MCP layer has no authentication:
keep the port local or restrict access at the network/proxy level.

Paste into your MCP client config (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, Zed, etc.):

{Snippet}
msg.stdio_creds1: Credentials — from the profile (dd-mcp login), or add to the env entry:
msg.stdio_footer: For HTTP clients (e.g. ChatGPT): dd-mcp print-config --http 127.0.0.1:8080

flag.local_only: don't revoke the device on the server, only forget the profile

err.nothing_to_forget: nothing to forget: no profile "{Name}" and DISCODRIVE_SERVER/DISCODRIVE_TOKEN are not set

msg.revoke_failed:
warning: failed to revoke the device on the server: {Err}
revoke it manually in the DiscoDrive web UI (the "Devices" section).
msg.env_only_nothing: No local profile (running via env variables) — nothing to forget.

err.refuse_no_token: refusing to bind {Addr} without authentication — a non-loopback address requires --http-token (or DISCODRIVE_HTTP_TOKEN). Use 127.0.0.1 for local-only, or set a token.

msg.exposed: dd-mcp: HTTP transport on {Addr} — EXPOSED TO THE NETWORK, bearer-token auth required. Clients must send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Prefer a reverse proxy with TLS.
msg.local: dd-mcp: HTTP transport on {Addr}. The MCP layer has no authentication — keep the port local.
msg.local_auth: dd-mcp: HTTP transport on {Addr} (loopback), bearer-token auth enabled.

flag.allow_changes: allow changing tools (delete files/contacts/events/tasks/radio/subscriptions, move/rename, mark tasks, update book metadata, have the server fetch URLs: save pages, downloads, radio, podcasts)
flag.http: start the HTTP transport on an address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080); default: stdio. The MCP layer has no authentication — keep the port local
flag.http_token: require this bearer token on the HTTP transport (Authorization: Bearer <token>); mandatory for non-loopback addresses. Fallback env: DISCODRIVE_HTTP_TOKEN
flag.lang: output language (en/de/es/fr/ru/sr/uk); default: from the environment

dd_files_list.desc: List of the contents of a DiscoDrive folder by path.

dd_files_read.desc: Read the contents of a DiscoDrive file as text. Text only — to download a binary file intact use the local CLI: dd-cli get <dd-path>.

dd_files_search.desc: Find files/folders by a name substring (recursively).

dd_files_upload.desc: Upload a text file to DiscoDrive by path. Text only: binary content passed here (images, archives, PDF) will be corrupted — upload binaries with the local CLI instead: dd-cli put <local-file> <dd-path>.

dd_files_mkdir.desc: Create a folder in DiscoDrive by path.

dd_files_delete.desc: Delete a DiscoDrive file/folder (not irreversible in the usual sense — goes to the trash).

dd_files_move.desc: Move a DiscoDrive node to another folder.

dd_calendar_events.desc: Calendar events in the window [start, end] (RFC3339, both required).

dd_calendar_create_event.desc: Create an event in a DiscoDrive calendar (location, description, all-day, repeat, reminder). Times must carry an explicit zone or Z.

dd_contacts_delete.desc: Delete a DiscoDrive contact by uid.

dd_calendar_delete_event.desc: Delete a calendar event by uid.

dd_tasks_delete.desc: Delete a DiscoDrive task by uid.

dd_tasks_set_done.desc: Mark a task as done/not done.

dd_music_list.desc: Contents of the DiscoDrive music folder (artists/albums/tracks as files); subpath descends inward.

dd_music_radio_add.desc: Add a radio station to DiscoDrive.

dd_music_podcast_add.desc: Subscribe to a podcast by RSS feed URL.

dd_books_list.desc: DiscoDrive book library with filters (q/author/series/genre, pagination via start).

dd_books_meta.desc: Book metadata by node-id (the nodeId field from dd_books_list).

dd_music_radio_delete.desc: Delete a radio station by id.

dd_music_podcast_delete.desc: Unsubscribe from a podcast by id.

dd_books_meta_update.desc: Update book metadata (full overwrite) by node-id.

dd_bookmarks_list.desc: Browser bookmarks stored in DiscoDrive. Returns a flat list; every item carries its folder path (for example "Toolbar/Dev") and its parent_id. q filters by title, url or path; folder_id limits the result to one subtree; folders_only returns just the folders. Large collections are truncated — narrow the query instead of raising the limit.

dd_bookmarks_add.desc: Create a bookmark, or a bookmark folder when is_folder is true (a folder has no url). parent_id must be the id of an existing folder from dd_bookmarks_list; leave it empty for the top level.

dd_bookmarks_update.desc: Rename a bookmark or folder, change its url, or move it into another folder. Only the fields you pass are changed; pass the literal "root" as parent_id to move it to the top level. Moving a folder into its own subtree is rejected.

dd_bookmarks_delete.desc: Delete a bookmark or folder by id. Deleting a folder also deletes everything inside it, and bookmarks have no trash — unlike files, this cannot be undone.

dd_pocket_list.desc: Read-later articles saved to DiscoDrive, newest first. Filter by status (pending, processing, done or error) and by q (substring of the title or the url). Server-side downloads never appear here — poll them with dd_download_status.

dd_pocket_read.desc: Read a saved article as markdown by its id from dd_pocket_list. Only items with status "done" and has_content true have a body. Long articles are truncated — page through them with offset and max_chars.

dd_pocket_add.desc: Save a web page to read later. The server fetches and converts it in the background, so the item starts as pending — check back with dd_pocket_list. Saving a url that is already saved does nothing, except that a failed one is retried; the title of an existing item cannot be changed.

dd_pocket_retry.desc: Fetch a saved article again by id: use it for items stuck in status "error", or to refresh a finished one. It fails while the item is still pending or processing.

dd_pocket_delete.desc: Remove a saved article by id. The markdown file already written into the Downloads folder is a normal file and stays there.

dd_download_add.desc: Ask the server to download a URL into the Downloads folder of the storage. The transfer runs on the server, not here, and returns an id with status pending. IMPORTANT: downloads are never listed anywhere — keep the id and poll dd_download_status. Adding the same url again retries it if it failed.

dd_download_status.desc: Progress of a server-side download, by the id returned from dd_download_add: status (pending, processing, done or error), bytes_done, size_bytes and the error text. This is the ONLY way to inspect a download — there is no list of downloads, and dd_pocket_list never shows them. Once it is done the file is in the Downloads folder, visible through dd_files_list.

dd_download_cancel.desc: Stop a running server-side download and forget its queue entry, by id. Bytes already written stay as a file in the Downloads folder — remove it with dd_files_delete if you do not want it.

dd_calendar_get_event.desc: Full details of a calendar event by uid: description, all-day flag, repeat and reminder.

dd_calendar_update_event.desc: Change an existing calendar event: only the fields given are written, an empty string clears a field.

msg.no_fields: nothing to change: pass at least one field
